inputs.share_count_basis: Cover-page basic 229.55M at 2026-07-31 (Q2 2026 10-Q, dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding) plus 4.0M dilutive share-based awards (Q2 2026 IncrementalCommonSharesAttributableToShareBasedPaymentArrangements) = 233.6M. The GAAP diluted weighted average (247.8M) also carries ~11.2M if-converted shares on the 2030 exchangeable notes; that $575M principal is already inside total_debt and the ~$51 conversion price is out of the money, so the notes are treated as debt and their shares EXCLUDED to avoid charging the instrument twice. Count held FLAT because SBC (incl. net-settlement taxes) is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income was $21.9M but MTCH is a net-DEBT company (net debt ~4.7x owner FCF), so no cash pile is being credited twice at the bridge; interest income is not stripped. Reported FCF is after $124.0M interest paid; the engine's component build is unlevered so this is irrelevant to the forward flows.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K: cash-flow SBC add-back $258.2M plus $128.5M taxes paid on net-share settlement (financing). MTCH publishes no combined 'SBC related to equity awards' figure, so the two lines are summed per method section 1(a). This is probably conservative: the FY2023-24 tax line was only $6-11M and the FY2025/H1-26 jump ($128.5M / $92.5M) reflects a shift to net settlement rather than a new economic cost; up to ~$100M/yr of the sum may be the same cost counted twice, worth roughly $4-5/share of PV. The forward sbc_pct_path is anchored at the FY2026 run-rate (SBC expense ~$240M post-13% headcount cut + ~$110M taxes = ~10% of revenue), not the 11.1% FY2025 print.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases $788.8M (10-K financing), H1-2026 $245.4M; diluted count down ~5% YoY. The flat count is being funded in cash by an active repurchaser; buybacks are value-neutral in this model (section 1) and are the mechanism by which the count stays flat. Dividend $0.19/qtr (~$186M FY2025) is a distribution, not modelled in the flows.
inputs.net_debt_note: Q2 2026 10-Q: LongTermDebt $3,551.9M (LongTermDebtCurrent 0 -- the remaining $423.9M of 0.875% 2026 exchangeables were repaid June 2026, cash fell $1,020M -> $581M) less cash $580.6M and short-term investments $3.2M = $2,968.1M. Operating lease liabilities (~$118M) are NOT added: ASC 842 operating lease cost sits inside EBITDA, so leases are charged in the flows.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Rf ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.3-1.4 => cost of equity ~10.7-11.2%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (blended senior notes/term loan), ~3.6% after tax; capital structure ~26% debt at market (debt $3.55B vs equity ~$9.4B) => WACC ~8.8-9.2%. 9.0% used, identical across scenarios -- turnaround/category risk is charged once, through the scenario paths and weights, not through per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: ASC 842 operating leases: lease cost expensed inside EBITDA (in the flows); lease liabilities excluded from net debt. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 1: consumer-internet subscription operating company; no memory entry, first valuation). 10-year horizon FY2026-FY2035 because the owner-FCF margin is still moving (SBC% gliding down, EBITDA margin expanding on the restructuring) through year 5. FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year-end); FY2026 is forecast year 1 and is anchored to the Q2 2026 guidance update (revenue near the midpoint of February guidance ~flat YoY; Adj EBITDA margin >37.5%; Tinder Direct Revenue -LSD; Hinge double-digit toward $1B by 2027; E&E -mid-teens). FY2025 Adj EBITDA reconstructed from XBRL: operating income $872.5M + SBC $258.2M + depreciation $67.1M + intangibles amortization ~$42M + impairment $0.1M = ~$1,240M (35.6% margin); H1-2026 ran ~39%. Price is a regular close, not after-hours. Cash tax ramps from 18% (FY2025 cash taxes were 13% of pretax on timing; GAAP ETR 17.8% with FDII/SBC deductions) to 21%. Working-capital capture set to 0: deferred revenue has been flat-to-declining ($252.7M FY2022 -> $151.3M FY2025 -> $152.7M Q2-26) as mix shifts to shorter-tenor and a la carte, so there is no bookings tailwind to capture.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case long-run revenue growth (FY2028-FY2035 average); equity CAGR undefined and EPS CAGR unusable, see notes
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR cannot be computed: shareholders' equity is NEGATIVE (-$1,413M FY2020 -> -$254M FY2025 -> -$237M Q2-26) following the 2020 IAC separation and $3.5B of cumulative buybacks. EPS CAGRs (25-28%) are distorted by one-offs in the base years (FY2020 separation costs, FY2022 $441M Tinder-founders settlement and impairments) and overstate the underlying ~3% revenue trend. Revenue CAGR used as the anchor and then overridden by guidance.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes (interest income not stripped, net-debt company): FY2021 $670.0M, FY2022 $163.4M (depressed by the $441M litigation payment), FY2023 $591.4M, FY2024 $603.3M, FY2025 $636.9M. The 3-year owner-FCF CAGR (57%) is off the FY2022 trough and meaningless; on FY2021-FY2025 owner FCF fell 1.3%/yr while reported FCF rose 5.3%/yr -- the combined SBC + net-settlement tax charge grew from $162M to $387M, so an increasing share of reported FCF growth was paid for in stock. CAGR formula ((end/start)^(1/n))-1 on FY2020->FY2025 revenue $2,391M->$3,487M (5y) and FY2022->FY2025 $3,189M->$3,487M (3y).

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 ~flat per Q2-26 guidance (H1-26 +1.3% YoY, Q2 -1%). FY2027: Hinge reaches ~$1B (+~$170M) against Tinder -LSD (~-$50M) and E&E -mid-teens (~-$100M) => +2%. FY2028-30: Tinder payers back to growth from Q4-27, E&E decline moderates, Hinge +10-15% => 3%; taper to 2% terminal.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 35.6% actual, H1-26 ~39% with the $100M restructuring in the run-rate; FY2026 guided >37.5% with H2 marketing seasonality => 38.0%, then 39% mature. No further step-up: app-store fees and Tinder marketing reinvestment cap the upside.
base.sbc_rationale: Combined SBC + net-settlement tax at ~10% of revenue in FY2026 (SBC expense trending ~$240M after the headcount cut, taxes ~$110M), gliding 0.3-0.4pp/yr to 7.0% as grants normalise post-turnaround -- slower than the 0.5pp default because the company has shown no commitment to a lower SBC run-rate.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax 18% rising to 21% statutory by year 4 (FY2025 cash 13% of pretax was timing; GAAP ETR 18-19%).

bull.rationale: Tinder payers return to growth on schedule (Q4-27) and compound LSD thereafter; Hinge passes $1B in 2027 and keeps 15-20% growth through 2029 on international expansion; E&E decline moderates to -5%. Margin reaches 42% on operating leverage plus a lower app-store take after further user-choice-billing wins. SBC glides to 6%.

bear.rationale: The last three years continue: Tinder payers/DAU keep falling mid-single digits as Gen Z disengages from swipe apps, the Q4-27 payer-growth milestone slips, Hinge growth decelerates toward 10% as it saturates its core markets, E&E keeps shrinking mid-teens. Revenue declines ~2.5%/yr through 2028, margin deleverages to 34% as marketing is held to defend Tinder, SBC is sticky in dollars so rises as a % of revenue.

scenario_narratives.base: Match is a mature, cash-generative portfolio whose consolidated top line is roughly flat: Hinge (~20% of revenue, +22% YoY) scales to $1B in 2027 and offsets a low-single-digit Tinder decline and a mid-teens E&E decline. The restructuring ($100M annualised savings, 13% headcount cut) lifts the adjusted EBITDA margin from 35.6% (FY2025) to ~39%, but the owner's view is weaker than the street's because SBC plus net-settlement taxes (~10% of revenue) is charged in full. Tinder payers return to growth around Q4-27 as management guides, giving ~3% consolidated growth in 2028-30 before tapering to 2%. Value is driven by the margin and SBC paths, not growth; the 2.97B of net debt takes ~25% of enterprise value.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Tinder turnaround works: the rebrand, Events (75 cities by end-2026) and AI-accelerated product cadence turn the DAU trend positive, payers grow from Q4-27 and compound low-single-digits; Hinge becomes a ~$1.5B franchise by 2029 on European/Latin American expansion and new monetisation tiers; E&E's decline moderates to -5%. Consolidated revenue grows 5-6% in 2028-29, margin reaches 42% with operating leverage and lower app-store fees after further user-choice-billing wins, and SBC glides to 6% of revenue. The terminal value is capped at 15x FCF rather than Gordon.
scenario_narratives.bear: Dating-app fatigue is structural, not cyclical. Tinder's payer and DAU declines do not stabilise, the Q4-27 payer-growth milestone slips, and Hinge's growth decelerates toward 10% as it saturates its core relationship-minded cohort; E&E keeps shrinking mid-teens. Consolidated revenue falls ~2.5%/yr through 2028 and only stabilises in the 2030s at 1% growth. Margin deleverages to 34% as marketing spend is held to defend Tinder and SBC is sticky in dollars (rising to 8.5-10.5% of revenue). Net debt at ~3x a shrinking EBITDA leaves the equity as the residual claim on a slowly melting asset; buybacks continue but at a lower pace.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% default because the bear case is a continuation of the observed three-year Tinder payer/DAU trend rather than a tail event, the turnaround's proof point (Tinder payer growth) is still over a year away, and ~half of revenue depends on it. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right at once -- Tinder payer growth on schedule, Hinge sustaining 15-20% growth beyond $1B, and margin expanding a further 400bp on top of the restructuring. Base at 50%: flat revenue with the restructuring margin in the run-rate is what the Q2-26 guidance already describes.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Match is valued as a mature subscription cash machine with a declining core and one growth asset. The headline (house) value expenses SBC and net-settlement taxes in full and holds the share count flat, so buybacks are the funding of a flat count rather than per-share growth; the street basis treating SBC as non-cash is reported alongside as the accounting-regime band. Leverage is charged once at the bridge (net debt $2.97B, exchangeables treated as debt and their if-converted shares excluded). WACC is the same in all three scenarios; turnaround and category risk is carried by the scenario paths and a 30% bear weight. The terminal cap (15x FCF) stops Gordon from rewarding a 2.5% perpetual growth assumption for a business whose largest brand has shrunk for three years.
key_risks_to_valuation: Tinder (~49% of revenue) payer and DAU declines continuing past the Q4-27 return-to-growth guidance -- each year of delay removes roughly 1pp of consolidated growth and 50-100bp of margin
SBC basis: summing the cash-flow SBC add-back and net-settlement taxes may double-count up to ~$100M/yr; the street band shows how much value depends on SBC treatment
App-store platform fees (15-30% of Direct Revenue) and adverse regulatory outcomes; conversely user-choice-billing wins are the main margin upside
Hinge growth decelerating before it reaches $1B as its core cohort saturates
Net debt ~2.4x adjusted EBITDA with the 2027-2031 senior-note ladder; refinancing cost rises if EBITDA shrinks (bear case) while buybacks and the dividend continue
Terminal value is 50-55% of enterprise value at a 9% WACC; a 1pp move in WACC moves the base value materially (see sensitivity grid)
